title: Naughty Dog Veteran Says GTA 6's Dynamic Lighting Feels Like "Alien Technology"

content:
Grand Theft Auto 6 has drawn praise from experienced game developers, including a veteran of Naughty Dog who described the scale of Rockstar’s work as difficult to comprehend.

Barclay, now world design director on Naughty Dog’s Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, compared the game’s apparent technical ambition to a Bugatti Veyron appearing before a “nervous Victorian child.” He said the comparison reflected his reaction after 19 years in the games industry. The Veyron can accelerate from zero to 100 kilometres per hour in a claimed 2.5 seconds; Barclay’s deliberately absurd image suggested that a Victorian child would need elaborate mechanical help to approach anything similar.

In a separate post, Barclay singled out Rockstar’s environmental lighting. He said he was impressed that much of it appeared to be dynamic while looking as good as, or better than, lighting created through pre-baked techniques. He also praised the game’s overcast scenes, saying the realistic appearance of cloudy-day lighting could make him stop and simply look at the streets.

Tim Soret, head of Odd Tales, the studio behind The Last Night, echoed Barclay’s assessment. He called the work “alien technology” and said it was difficult to comprehend.

Barclay has worked across several studios and projects during his career. His credits include Star Wars: Battlefront 3 at Free Radical Design and The Shoot at Cohort Studios, followed by years at Crytek and Cloud Imperium Games. He joined Naughty Dog in 2016. On his blog, he has written in detail about the development of The Last of Us Part 2, as well as other games and design ideas.

The praise adds to the attention surrounding GTA 6’s visual presentation and technical ambitions. The supplied report describes the game as an exceptionally high-fidelity open-world experience and cites early estimates of about 25 million copies sold and $2.36 billion in gross revenue. It also says the game’s Metacritic score places it among the highest-rated games of all time. These figures and rankings were presented as estimates or reported assessments, rather than official sales figures from Rockstar or its parent company, Take-Two.
